title: Regions, availability zones and paired regions

videos.script: You are about to work on Azure for twenty-six lessons. You will not need an Azure account for any of them. {{lab}} Your own computer is the lab. It holds the real Azure command line, the Bicep compiler and Terraform. {{tools}} None of them pretends to be Azure. They check what you write, and they refuse what only Azure could answer. {{refuse}} This lesson builds that lab, step by step, and shows what to do when a step fails. Then it asks a first question. Where is Azure? {{map}} Azure is a set of regions, each one a place on the map. São Paulo is one, and this course works there. {{zones}} Inside the region sit availability zones. A zone has its own power, its own cooling and its own network. You spread a system across zones so that it survives losing one. {{mapping}} But zone one is a label, not a building. Two subscriptions can mean two different places by it. {{pairs}} Most regions also have a pair. São Paulo's pair is in Texas, and that decides where some of your data goes. {{prices}} Last, every boundary data crosses has a price per gigabyte. You will read those prices yourself, from the list Microsoft publishes. {{end}}
